_why_this_exists_before_the_review_does: AUT-PROP-006. This record is written as the seat's FIRST act, so a seat that dies leaves evidence that it looked rather than nothing at all. It is EMPTY and says so: publish_bar.clause_1_hardening_converged REFUSES any round with an open record at the commit it is grading, because an unfinished look must never be counted as a clean one.
central_claim: On one US trial registry, patients with an ultra-rare fusion-driven sarcoma (EMC) are eligible for recruiting trials whose listed-conditions field never names the histology, because eligibility is written on the molecular lesion while the field a condition search reads is written on histology; and because a keyword-built reachability map would carry two adjudicated refusals as false positives, eligibility text has to be read one trial at a time.

blockers.summary: §3 attributes a yield of TWO treatment-admitting trials to the four-record adjudication. The committed adjudication produced ONE. The second admitting interventional trial (NCT05918640) was not adjudicated on 2026-08-09 at all — it was carried in from the 2026-08-07 re-verification of a prior memo — so the sentence misstates the sample the headline count was drawn from.
blockers.evidence: Paper §3, after the table: 'Two trials admit and offer treatment; a third admits and offers enrolment in an observational cohort. Those are counts of the four records adjudicated here, not of the registry.' The committed artifact research/literature/emc-trial-reachability-adjudication-2026-08-09.json names exactly four adjudicated records (NCT06571734, NCT04151342, NCT06094101, NCT07188532 — its `closes` field says it closes fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json → task_2_widened_search.candidates_requiring_eligibility_text_verification, whose four members are those NCTs) and its `summary` reads "candidates_adjudicated": 4, "admits_and_is_interventional": 1, "admits_but_is_observational": 1, "refused": 2, with the verbatim finding 'Two of the four admit, and only one of those two offers treatment.' NCT05918640 appears nowhere in that file; in the 2026-08-07 artifact it sits in task_1_reverification_of_section_3_3 and task_2_widened_search.confirmed_fusion_family_defined with retrieved_from.source_url = 'https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT05918640?format=json'. No reading rescues the sentence: the table's four ROWS are not four records either (row 3 is nine records the paper itself calls 'not adjudicated'), and §5 uses the same phrase with the correct numerator — 'Four candidates were adjudicated: two admit, one of them observationally, and two refuse.'
blockers.fix: Replace the last sentence of that paragraph with one that names the actual denominator, e.g. 'Those counts are over the five records adjudicated in this paper — the four candidates re-fetched on 2026-08-09 and NCT05918640, confirmed on 2026-08-07 — not over the registry.' No count changes; only the population the counts are said to cover.

blockers.summary: §5 describes the screens that built the candidate pool as 'keyword screens on titles, conditions and interventions' and infers from that description that a trial whose fusion language lives only in eligibility text 'could never enter the pool'. The committed manifest shows two of the three screens are free-text `query.term` searches, and the same artifact contains direct evidence that `query.term` reaches fields well beyond title, condition and intervention. The field list in those URLs is a RETURN-field selector, not a search scope. The stated limitation therefore rests on a false description of the instrument.
blockers.evidence: research/literature/emc-clinical-sweep-c3.json: ct_fusion_recruiting_fixed = 'https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies?query.term=%22gene+fusion%22+OR+%22fusion-positive%22+OR+%22FET+fusion%22+OR+%22translocation%22&filter.overallStatus=RECRUITING&pageSize=400&format=json&fields=NCTId%7CBriefTitle%7COverallStatus%7CPhase%7CInterventionName%7CCondition%7CStudyType'; ct_basket_recruiting_fixed is the same shape; ct_sarcoma_recruiting_fixed = 'query.cond=soft+tissue+sarcoma...pageSize=1000' — a CONDITION-only search that never touched titles or interventions, and the screen that actually found the headline trial NCT06571734 (its retrieved_from.source_url in fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json). That `query.term` searches beyond the three named fields is proved inside the same artifact: task_2_widened_search.nr4a3_is_absent_from_the_registry_index.search_url is 'https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies?query.term=NR4A3&pageSize=100&format=json' and its five returned studies (NCT00733200, NCT02968888, NCT03033953, NCT03139344, NCT05447338) carry no 'NR4A3' string in brief_title, official_title, listed_conditions or interventions — e.g. NCT05447338 is conditions ['Neck Pain'], interventions all myofascial-induction procedures. The paper itself states the same fact two bullets earlier: 'The registry's free-text search reads fields beyond the conditions list.'
blockers.fix: Rewrite the bullet to describe the instruments as committed and stop the inference at what is measured: 'Candidates entered the pool through two free-text term screens (fusion, basket) and one condition screen on soft tissue sarcoma. Which fields the registry's term search covers is not established here — it demonstrably reaches beyond conditions and interventions, since the driver-gene term search returned trials carrying the gene in neither — so we cannot say whether a trial whose only fusion language sits in its eligibility text could enter the pool. The fusion screen returned 400 of a 400-record page and is truncated, which is what makes the counts floors.'

p1s.summary: The staleness limitation names one stale status flag among the nine molecularly-defined records, but six of those nine carry NO status-verified date in the record at all, because the fields-limited basket screen never requested one. The bullet therefore bounds an exposure that is unmeasured for two-thirds of the group.
p1s.evidence: Paper §5: 'Every status here is as posted on the retrieval date, and one of the nine, the basket trial NCT03767075, carried a RECRUITING flag last verified in April 2024.' In fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json, task_2_widened_search.molecularly_defined_not_histology_defined: NCT05768178, NCT05770037, NCT05770102, NCT05770544, NCT05786716 and NCT07440290 each have "status_verified_date": null and "last_update_post_date": null, all with retrieved_from.source_url = the ct_basket_recruiting_fixed URL whose `fields=` list omits statusVerifiedDate. NCT03767075 = '2024-04' and NCT06988475 = '2025-11' are the only dated ones besides NCT05722886 ('2026-06'). That the nulls are field-limitation and not registry absence is provable from the pair: NCT06571734 is null in the 2026-08-07 fielded screen and 'status_verified_date': '2026-06' once re-fetched individually in emc-trial-reachability-adjudication-2026-08-09.json. The same gap exists for three of the four adjudicated records, where only NCT06571734 carries a status_verified_date and the file's own _limits says 'Each record's statusVerifiedDate is quoted where the payload carried one.'
p1s.fix: Add the measured shape to the bullet: 'one of the nine, NCT03767075, carried a RECRUITING flag last verified in April 2024; six of the nine were read through a fields-limited screen that returned no verification date at all, so their staleness is unmeasured rather than recent.'

p1s.summary: The paper's core absence — 'a condition search on their own diagnosis does not return' these trials — is established from each record's conditions FIELD, not from any committed record of what a diagnosis condition search actually returned. The two condition searches on the diagnosis were run once, were transport-damaged, were not re-run after the fix, and their return sets are enumerated nowhere.
p1s.evidence: Every 'EMC listed? no' cell traces to emc_in_listed_conditions:false in fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json / listed_conditions in the 2026-08-09 adjudication. The two diagnosis searches exist — emc-clinical-sweep-targets.json ct_emc_all = 'query.cond=extraskeletal+myxoid+chondrosarcoma&pageSize=100' and ct_myxoid_chondrosarcoma = 'query.cond=myxoid+chondrosarcoma&pageSize=100' — but the artifact records only their FAILURES (transport_integrity.unparseable_records lists NCT00720174/NCT05355753 and NCT00720174/NCT05355753/NCT01189253 under those two payloads) and never their return sets; task_2_widened_search.instruments describes them only as returning 'every study whose CONDITION list names EMC'. The paper states the searches 'were not re-run after the fix'. So no committed artifact shows a diagnosis condition search executing and NOT returning NCT05918640 or NCT06571734; the step from 'the histology is absent from the conditions field' to 'the search does not return it' is the paper's §1 model, not a measurement.
p1s.fix: Say which observation carries the absence: 'Absence here is measured on the listed-conditions field of each retrieved record, which §1 identifies as the field a condition search matches; the return set of a condition search on the diagnosis is not itself committed, and those two searches were not re-run after the transport fix.'

p1s.summary: The abstract's warrant for 'two is a floor' attaches saturation to the screens that found the two admitting trials. Neither of them came from the saturated screen.
p1s.evidence: Abstract: 'the screens that found them match keywords and one of them saturated, so two is a floor.' In fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json, NCT05918640.retrieved_from.source_url is the per-NCT URL 'https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT05918640?format=json' (a targeted re-verification of a record already cited in an earlier memo — task_1's own _readme), and NCT06571734.retrieved_from.source_url is the sarcoma condition screen 'query.cond=soft+tissue+sarcoma...pageSize=1000', which task_2_widened_search.instruments records as returning 526 — well under its page limit. The screen that saturated is ct_fusion_recruiting_fixed (pageSize=400, 'returns': '400 recruiting studies...'), and the records it found are NCT07188532, NCT06094101 and NCT04151342 — the two refusals and the observational cohort. §5's fuller statement is the correct one, because truncation of the POOL is what makes the counts floors; the abstract's compression is not.
p1s.fix: Reattach the saturation to the pool: '...and the pool they were drawn from was built by keyword screens, one of which came back at its page limit, so two is a floor.'

p1s.summary: §4.1 says one query ran on the UK registry; two did. And the two registries are compared on findings produced by non-comparable instruments — 1,159 indexed studies through fusion/basket/sarcoma screens on one side, three records from two queries on the other — which the paper does not state when it concludes 'the mechanism therefore runs in both directions'.
p1s.evidence: Paper §4.1: 'the query that ran there was the parent term chondrosarcoma, and it returns two trials'. research/literature/non-us-registry-sweep-2026-08-09.json endpoints[0] records "registry": "ISRCTN (UK)", "queries": ["chondrosarcoma", "sarcoma AND fusion"], and isrctn_what_it_holds carries both query_chondrosarcoma (total_count 2) and query_sarcoma_and_fusion (total_count 1, ISRCTN52235823, a diagnostic methylome study), which the paper never mentions. Against that, retrieval.unique_studies_indexed = 1159 on the US side. So 'In the non-US registry read here the disease appears only as an exclusion' is a within-registry universal drawn from three records returned by two queries, and no ISRCTN instrument comparable to the 400-record fusion screen was run — an admitting-but-not-naming trial there is something the search design had little power to detect. §5 bounds the GEOGRAPHIC generalisation ('not shown to generalise') but says nothing about the asymmetry of the instruments.
p1s.fix: State both: 'Two queries ran there — the parent term chondrosarcoma, returning two trials, and sarcoma AND fusion, returning one diagnostic study. Those three records are the whole of what was read in that registry, against 1,159 indexed on the US side, so the direction of the mechanism there is what three records show and not a property of the registry.'

p2s.summary: §2's table attributes '1,159 unique studies indexed' to the four screens it names; the artifact's number is the union over all four CI runs and every payload in them.
p2s.evidence: fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json retrieval.unique_studies_indexed = 1159 sits above a `runs` list of four slugs whose manifests include the two diagnosis condition searches, the EWSR1 term search, the unfielded frontier sarcoma screen and a dozen per-NCT fetches. The four screens the paper names sum to 400+199+526+5 = 1,130 before any de-duplication, so the union of just those cannot be 1,159.

p2s.summary: §5's 'Every absence reported here is an absence from a condition search' is contradicted by §3's driver-gene absence, which came from a term search — as the same bullet then says.
p2s.evidence: §3: 'A term search for the driver gene returns five studies... No trial that search returns is indexed to this disease's driver.' The search is task_2_widened_search.nr4a3_is_absent_from_the_registry_index.search_url = 'query.term=NR4A3&pageSize=100'. The bullet's own next sentence names it: 'the driver-gene term search returned trials whose listed conditions are neck pain and spinal-cord injury.'

p2s.summary: §7 names two manifest paths that do not exist at this commit, and omits the manifest behind the unfielded sarcoma screen §2 relies on.
p2s.evidence: §7: 'The URL manifests behind the 2026-08-07 sweep are research/literature/emc-clinical-sweep-targets.json, -c3.json and -c4.json'. `git show <SHA>:research/literature/emc-clinical-sweep-targets-c3.json` fails; the committed files are research/literature/emc-clinical-sweep-c3.json and -c4.json (no '-targets'). The 2026-08-07 artifact's retrieval.runs lists a FOURTH manifest, research/manuscripts/modality-census/lit-targets-frontier-capability-2026-08-07.json, which is where ct_sarcoma_2026_new lives — the unfielded screen §2 credits with carrying eligibility text and the source of one of the 'three of those nine'.

p2s.summary: The abstract's 'One recruiting trial does list the histology' is true of the records read, but two further records in the same artifact also list it; a reader sizing findability sees one example where the artifact holds three.
p2s.evidence: In fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json task_1, emc_in_listed_conditions is true for NCT06239272 (RECRUITING, 42 conditions), NCT05836571 (ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING, conditions include 'Locally Advanced Extraskeletal Myxoid Chondrosarcoma') and NCT03600649 (overall_status 'UNKNOWN', status_verified_date 2023-11, 11 conditions). Only the first is RECRUITING, so the sentence is defensible; neither of the other two is mentioned anywhere in the paper, and an 'UNKNOWN' status is a stale recruiting flag rather than a closure.

p2s.summary: Front matter and abstract describe the read dates differently.
p2s.evidence: Front-matter scope: 'Two public trial registries — one US, one UK — read on two dates'. Abstract: 'We read one public registry twice and a second one once'. non-us-registry-sweep-2026-08-09.json _retrieval.date_et is '2026-08-09' only, so the abstract is the accurate one.

p2s.summary: 'Interventional' for NCT05918640 is inferred, not read from a recorded field.
p2s.evidence: The 2026-08-09 adjudication records "study_type": "INTERVENTIONAL" for NCT06571734 and "OBSERVATIONAL" for NCT04151342. Neither artifact records a study_type for NCT05918640; what is recorded is phases ['PHASE1','PHASE2'] and interventions ['Lurbinectedin']. The inference is safe on ClinicalTrials.gov conventions, but it is an inference and the abstract's 'two recruiting interventional trials' rests on it.

objections_i_raised_and_the_paper_alread: That the age bound '1 to 30 at the diagnostic biopsy' for NCT06239272 might be transport-damaged, since that record carries removal_markers_in_eligibility_text = 9 and an age criterion is exactly a comparison-operator sentence. The artifact records the quoted sentence verbatim as 'Patients must be 1-30 years at the time of the biopsy that established the diagnosis of NRSTS' with verbatim_sentence_is_transport_clean = true.

That the transport-loss arithmetic in §2 might not reconcile. It reconciles exactly: the union of transport_integrity.silently_damaged_records and unparseable_records is 12 distinct NCTs; five of them (NCT05836571, NCT07695311, NCT07188532, NCT05275426, NCT06094101) appear as complete records elsewhere in the same file; of the remaining seven, exactly three (NCT00720174, NCT05355753, NCT01189253) came from the two diagnosis condition searches, and emc-hypoxia-therapeutic-status.json gives them as COMPLETED, TERMINATED and TERMINATED — 'one completed and two terminated'.

That the driver-gene absence might be presented as a registry census. §3 refuses the census explicitly: 'no total was recorded: five is what it returned, not what the registry holds', and the claim it draws is bounded to the returned set.

That the fusion-partner ordering might be a remembered figure. task_2_widened_search._supporting_literature_read_in_the_same_ci_run carries the review's verbatim ('over 70%' EWSR1, 'about 20%' TAF15, '<5%' FUS/TCF12/TFG) and flags it SECONDARY; the paper states the ordering and claims no percentage.

That the refusing non-US endpoints might be counted as absences. Both the abstract and §5 say a refusal states what an endpoint would answer and never what a registry contains, and the WHO 404 is reported as this sweep's own URL defect rather than a finding.

That the jRCT TLS failure might be over-read as an endpoint policy. The artifact's positive-control block does read it that way; the paper is stricter than its own artifact — 'a handshake failure is not separable from a fault of our own'.
That the observational cohort might be counted alongside treatment trials. §3 holds NCT04151342 out in its own row and says why, matching the adjudication's 'admits_but_is_observational'.

That '§4's two refusals would have passed a keyword screen' might be an untested counterfactual. Both NCT06094101 and NCT07188532 entered this study's own pool through the fusion keyword screen (retrieved_from.source_url = ct_fusion_recruiting_fixed), so they demonstrably did pass one.
notes: On this lens the paper's central claim survives: the two admitting trials, the keyword-trap counter-finding and the bounded driver-gene absence are each carried by fields I could quote from the committed artifacts, and the paper is repeatedly more conservative than its own sources (the transport-loss arithmetic reconciles exactly, the NR4A3 search is refused as a census, the TLS failure is not read as a policy, the observational cohort is held out of the treatment count). What fails is the description of the SAMPLE and the INSTRUMENT. §3 credits the four-record adjudication with two treatment-admitting trials when the adjudication artifact records one and names the second nowhere; §5 describes two free-text term screens as searches 'on titles, conditions and interventions' and then draws a coverage limit from that description, when the same artifact's NR4A3 result proves the term search reaches beyond those fields and the third screen searched conditions alone. Both are provenance errors rather than count errors — every headline number is right — but both tell a reader that a figure covers a population it does not, which is the failure this lens exists to catch. The four P1s are of one family: a bound stated where the underlying reading is missing (six of nine status dates never retrieved), an absence measured on a field rather than on the search it stands for, saturation attached to screens that did not saturate, and a two-registry comparison whose two arms were probed with instruments three orders of magnitude apart.
